invariants: Every new or changed English string gets a Welsh draft beside it in the same change, as the service's other copy does.

Every changed page works fully without JavaScript: every state change is a form post, every search and filter a form with a button that submits it, and JavaScript only enhances a page that already works (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm claim 6; conflicts:c-006).

A behaviour is built with GOV.UK Frontend first, then another tested government library (Ministry of Justice, HMRC, Scottish Government); no custom JavaScript is written to copy the prototype, pop-ups are not built and confirmations stay pages (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm claims 5, 7 and 19).
Pages are built from GOV.UK Frontend components and govuk-* classes; the prototype's custom app-dr2-* blocks are not copied.

A search box is the real frontend's accessible autocomplete over a native select and behaves as the real frontend configures it; its entries are what MDM serves through reference-data, and only how the list reads follows the prototype (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm claims 1 to 4).

Where a row changes a page or behaviour the high-risk plants frontend also has, the same increment changes plants too: plants mirrors the structure, wording patterns, components and behaviour, and keeps its own questions, data and step order (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm claims 43 and 44).
Shared wording in a frontend's shared copy is never reworded in place; a set-specific string goes in the feature's own copy (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm claim 41).

Notification statuses are only ever added, never renamed or removed, and each new status is mapped in every frontend that reads it before the animals backend first sends it (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm claim 42).
A page in its error state keeps the 'Error: ' prefix on its browser title (conflicts:c-006).

Save and return to overview makes exactly the same checks as Save and continue on every page that has both buttons, in live animals, germinal products, templates and high-risk plants: the trader sees an error for each answer the page refuses and stays on the page with what they entered kept; with none, the answers are saved (ruling:sam-2026-10-26 claims 1 and 2; replaces conflicts c-211 and c-313).
Notifications, templates and address book entries stay scoped to the signed-in user's organisation (or user, for templates); nothing lists another organisation's records.
Each increment updates the tests repo's specs, page objects and journey helpers its change breaks, in the same change.

increments.title: Ask 'What are you importing?' before a notification is created
increments.detail: Starting a new notification from the all-types dashboard in the INS front door (today's INS home) asks the notification type question first, before any draft exists. Live animals carries on to the animals frontend's live-animals start, which creates the GBN-AG draft and lands on origin. Germinal products, offered second under the 9 October ruling, carries on to the start of the germinal products set, the live-animals set's sibling in the animals frontend; the ruling lets this link land before the set itself is built. Plants for planting, Potatoes (seed and ware) and Wood products carry on to the start of the high-risk plants journey in trade-imports-plants-frontend, which creates a plants draft and lands on plants' own first page. Abandoning the question leaves no empty draft behind. Every hand-over goes to the receiving service's address as each environment configures it, so it works on the deployed environments, the local stack and the CI stack, including for a user not yet signed in to the receiving service.
acceptanceCriteria: Starting a new notification from the INS home shows the question 'What are you importing?' instead of going straight to an origin page, and no draft notification is created at that point: the dashboard's notification list gains no new entry while the question is open or after the user leaves it with Back (prototype:dr2-1-source app/routes.js:11112-11114; trace:prototype-dr2-1 T1; trace:e2e T01 call@286; ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm p3-063; conflicts:c-007)

The notification type page has the browser title 'What are you importing? - Import notification service - GOV.UK' and the heading 'What are you importing?' as the radios' fieldset legend (h1), with the caption 'About the consignment' inside the heading (prototype:dr2-1-source app/views/design-release-2.1/notification-type.html:7,39; trace:prototype-dr2-1 T1 action 16)

The question offers radios in this order, with no hint text on the group or any option and none pre-selected: Live animals; Germinal products (semen, ova, embryos); Plants for planting; Potatoes (seed and ware); Wood products (prototype:dr2-1-source app/routes.js:125-131; trace:prototype-dr2-1 T1 action 16; ruling:sam-2026-10-09 p1-048, p1-052; conflicts:c-007)

Choosing Live animals and pressing Continue creates a new live-animals draft and lands on its 'Origin of the import' page, which shows the Draft tag and a new GBN-AG reference (prototype:dr2-1-specs e2e/about-the-consignment.fit.spec.js:65; trace:prototype-dr2-1 T1 action 44; conflicts:c-007)

Choosing Germinal products (semen, ova, embryos) and pressing Continue sends the user from the INS front door to the germinal products set's start under /germinal-products in the animals frontend, and no live-animals notification is created: the dashboard's notification list gains no live-animals entry (ruling:sam-2026-10-09 p1-006, p1-048, p1-053; ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm p3-091; conflicts:c-007)

Choosing Plants for planting, Potatoes (seed and ware) or Wood products and pressing Continue lands on the first page of the high-risk plants journey in the plants service, with a new plants draft, and no live-animals notification is created (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-templates p1-039; conflicts:c-007)

Pressing Continue with nothing chosen re-shows the page with an error summary titled 'There is a problem' listing 'Select what you are importing', linked to the first radio, the same message shown inline on the radio group, and the browser title prefixed 'Error: ' (prototype:dr2-1-source app/routes.js:151-160; trace:prototype-dr2-1 T1 action 30; prototype:dr2-1-specs e2e/about-the-consignment.fit.spec.js:53-57; ruling:sam-2026-10-09 p1-106; conflicts:c-006)

The page ends with a single 'Continue' button: there is no 'Save and return to overview' button and no cancel link (prototype:dr2-1-source app/views/design-release-2.1/notification-type.html:48-53; trace:prototype-dr2-1 T1 action 16)

The page's Back link goes to the INS home, and the service navigation highlights Dashboard (prototype:dr2-1-source app/routes.js:10606-10608; trace:prototype-dr2-1 T1 action 15; ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm p3-085)

The page shows no Draft strip and no notification reference; the origin page reached after choosing Live animals shows both (prototype:dr2-1-source app/views/design-release-2.1/notification-type.html:23-57; trace:prototype-dr2-1 T1 action 16 against action 44; conflicts:c-007)

With Welsh chosen, every string on the notification type page (title, caption, heading, the five options, the error message and the Continue button) shows its Welsh counterpart (repo:frontend features/origin/copy/copy.cy.js:1-3)

Each hand-over from the question goes to the receiving service at the address that environment configures for it, never a fixed host, port or relative path: Live animals and Germinal products to the animals service, and the three plants types to the plants service. Each lands where the criteria above say on the deployed test environments, on the local stack and on the CI stack (ruling:sam-2026-11-04 links work in CDP, the local Docker stack and the CI Docker stack)

A user signed in to the INS front door but not yet to the receiving service who chooses a type and presses Continue goes through sign-in without the browser blocking any step, and lands on the same page with a new draft that an already-signed-in user would reach (ruling:sam-2026-11-04 links work in CDP, the local Docker stack and the CI Docker stack)

Re-analysis 4 November: nothing in this row is on main in any repo. Main SHAs: ins-frontend 9492bf8, animals 2038fc3a, plants ed29ede, tests ed3b378, workspace 4fcec603. The code it builds on has moved but not changed shape. Animals and plants createPost still run startJourney, then beginOpeningRun, then redirect to the first page (origin, commodity-type), reached only by crumb-protected POSTs, and neither serves a /start GET. The INS home still shows 'Start a new notification' only for an empty list, linking to the animals live-animals list. INS set bases still hold only /live-animals. No germinal-products set exists: Germinal still lands on a 404 under /germinal-products, which the 9 October ruling allows (ruling-sam-2026-10-09.md: 'Links to the germinal set landing on main before the set is built: ye thats fine'). No ruling since 9 October changes this row. The 26 October Save and return ruling does not apply: the page has only Continue. Two criteria are added, under Sam's standing requirement for this theme (4 November, cited as ruling:sam-2026-11-04; record it as a ruling file in sources/): the hand-overs work in CDP, the local stack and the CI stack, and they survive the trader not yet being signed in on the receiving service. The tests repo has retired @integration since the stale spec was written.

Cross-service config per environment, all on main except the Defra ID form-action origin. INS reads tradeImportsAnimalsFrontend.baseUrl (TRADE_IMPORTS_ANIMALS_FRONTEND_URL) and tradeImportsPlantsFrontend.baseUrl (TRADE_IMPORTS_PLANTS_FRONTEND_URL). Local stack and CI stack (the same docker/stack/frontend.compose.yml): http://localhost:3000 and http://localhost:3003. CDP dev, test and perf-test (cdp-app-config): https://trade-imports-animals-frontend.<env>.cdp-int.defra.cloud and https://trade-imports-plants-frontend.<env>.cdp-int.defra.cloud. The hand-over is a POST on INS redirecting to the start entry, and for a trader with no session there on to the Defra ID stub, so INS's CSP form-action must also allow the browser-facing stub origin: http://localhost:3007 in both stacks, https://trade-imports-defra-id-stub.<env>.cdp-int.defra.cloud in CDP. The stale branch's DEFRA_ID_FORM_ACTION_ORIGINS defaults to localhost:3007 and is set in neither compose nor cdp-app-config, so as written it passes locally and in CI and fails in CDP. Either set it explicitly in compose and have Sam add it to cdp-app-config for ins-frontend dev, test and perf-test (agents may not write CDP repos), or derive it from DEFRA_ID_OIDC_CONFIGURATION_URL through the existing defraId.signOutHostnameRewrite. That URL is already browser-facing in CDP, where the rewrite is off; in the stacks the rewrite maps host.docker.internal to localhost. Deriving it needs no new environment config. The plan picks one. No plants-to-INS link is added here, so plants' missing TRADE_IMPORTS_INS_FRONTEND_URL in CDP (for inc-150) does not affect this row.

Tests: the hand-over specs live in tests/ins/ and assert destinations by new URL(requireBaseUrl('TRADE_IMPORTS_*_FRONTEND_BASE_URL')).origin, with no literal hosts. They are not tagged @compose, so the CDP run covers them. Tag them @animals-frontend, and add a @plants-frontend tag to the trade-imports-plants-frontend entry in the workspace's config/e2e-tests-pr-scope.json, so animals and plants PRs run them. At least one hand-over test starts with no session on the receiving service. Locally, animals and plants share the yar cookie name 'session' on localhost, so a spec moving between those two in one browser context can clobber the session; INS is unaffected (ins-session).

Seen while checking, not a criterion: a plants type hands over to plants' commodity-type page, which also asks 'What are you importing?', with labels 'Potatoes (seed or ware)' and 'Wood and cut trees' against the question's 'Potatoes (seed and ware)' and 'Wood products'. increments.title: Back from a page opened by a review Change link goes to the previous journey page, in animals and plants
increments.detail: Every journey page's Back link follows how the page was reached. On a draft notification, a page opened from the review page's Change link goes Back to the previous page in the journey's step order, not to the review and not to Overview, and Save and continue there still returns to the review. The step order is the same one the opening-run Back links already follow. A step whose opening-run Back link is Overview keeps Overview. The journey's first page keeps the Back link it has without a Change link. The context comes from the service's own journey state, not from a from=review marker. Today, every page opened from a draft's review Change link goes Back to Overview, except animals Roles and addresses, which goes Back to the review. High-risk plants gets the same rule, in its own step order, at the same time as live animals. These stay as they are: upload documents goes Back to the review, an address view or edit opened from the review returns to it, and while a notification is being amended every page keeps its usual Back link.
acceptanceCriteria: In live animals, on a draft notification, a journey page opened from a Change link on the review page has a 'Back' link to the previous page in the step order, the page its opening-run Back link opens: Reason for import and Commodity details go back to What are you importing?, What are you importing? to Origin, Additional details to Animal identification or Commodity details, and Transit countries to Arrival details. A step whose opening-run Back link is Overview keeps Overview. The origin page keeps the Back link it has without a Change link. No such page, Roles and addresses included, goes Back to the review page. 'Save and continue' there still returns to the review page. (prototype:dr2-1-source app/routes.js:488-498, p1-052, p1-053; ruling:sam-2026-10-09 p1-089, p1-198; repo:frontend docs/journey-flow-and-gates.md:141-152, features/addresses/controller.js:75-78)

'Save and continue' there still returns to the review page. The commodity type page keeps today's Back link, because it is plants' first page. (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-templates p1-044, p1-049, p1-050; prototype:dr2-1-source p1-053; repo:plantsfrontend shared/kit.js:188-201, docs/journey-flow-and-gates.md:122-130)
